name: Kaiserklamm
kurzbeschreibung: The wildly romantic Kaiserklamm in Brandenberg enchants visitors with rushing whirlpools, a historic 1894 timber rafting path, and the historic Kaiserhaus.
oeffnungszeiten: Mai bis Ende Okt tagsüber frei zugänglich (bei Hochwasser und im Winter gesperrt)
beschreibung:
Overview

The Kaiserklamm is one of the most spectacular and pristine rocky gorges in Tirol. Located in the municipality of Brandenberg within the Kufstein district, the torrential Brandenberger Ache has carved its way deep into the hard limestone of the Brandenberger Alpen over thousands of years. With its foaming whirlpools, emerald-green plunge pools, and walkways boldly chiseled into vertical rock faces, the gorge constitutes a fascinating natural monument and an outstanding hiking destination in the holiday region of Alpbachtal.

History & Timber Rafting

The gorge owes its distinguished name to a historic event: in July 1894, Emperor Franz Joseph I. von Österreich personally visited the Brandenbergtal to marvel at the spectacular spectacle of alpine timber rafting. For over five centuries—from its first documented mention in 1492 until its final cessation in 1966—the Brandenberger Ache served as the region's vital artery for timber transport: hundreds of thousands of cubic metres of timber from dense mountain forests were drifted through the narrow gorge on surging wild waters down to Kramsach in the Inntal, supplying the local smelting works and salt mines. Today's approximately one-kilometre-long Triftsteig trail was originally carved into the cliff face by courageous log drivers who used long hook poles to dislodge jammed logs. Secured by solid railings and wire cables, the well-maintained path leads across bridges and through small rock tunnels directly above the foaming torrents. Located near the entrance of the gorge is the heritage-listed, over 500-year-old inn Kaiserhaus, where Empress Elisabeth ("Sisi") was once a guest.

Visit & Getting There

The Kaiserklamm is freely and openly accessible free of charge during daylight hours in the ice-free months from early May to late October (during heavy rainfall, flood events, and in winter, the path is officially closed for safety reasons). Pure walking time through the gorge: approx. 30 minutes (one way; sturdy footwear is strictly required). Arrival by car: via the Inntalautobahn A12, exit 32 Kramsach/Brixlegg, then along the Brandenberger Landesstraße L4 through Kramsach up to Brandenberg, continuing via Aschau to the large car park at Kaiserhaus (parking fee applies, approx. €5.00 per day). By public transport: by train to Bahnhof Brixlegg or Rattenberg-Kramsach, from there by VVT regional bus line 620 to Brandenberg, and in summer continuing with the Kaiserhaus hiking bus.

Tips

Due to narrow rock passages, stone steps, and damp wooden boardwalks, the gorge path is not suitable for wheelchairs or prams; safety harnesses are recommended for young children and can be hired at Kaiserhaus. Dogs must be kept on a short leash. Following the hike, a stop at Gasthaus Kaiserhaus is well worthwhile, world-renowned for its traditional Brandenberger Prügeltorte cake.
